segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Hello?

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Hi, Susie, it’s Paul here. How are you? Enjoying your new job? You’re working at the library, aren’t you?

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes. I started when the library re-opened a month ago . It’s great.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Actually Carol and I have been meaning to join for a while.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Oh, you should. It doesn’t cost anything, and the new library has all sorts of facilities. It’s not just a place where you borrow books. For instance, there’s an area with comfortable seats where you can sit and read the magazines they have there. Some people spend the whole morning there.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Mmm. Wish I had that amount of time to spend!

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes, you must be pretty busy at present, with the children and everything?

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: We are, yes. But we’re hoping to get away this summer. We’re thinking of going to Greece.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Well, we’ve got a much larger section of the library devoted to travel books now [[ ]] , so you should come and have a look. I can’t remember if there’s anything specifically on Greece, but I should think so.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: OK. Now Carol’s organising a project for the history class she teaches at school – it’s about life in the town a hundred years ago. Do you have anything that might be useful?

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes, actually we’ve now got a new section with materials on the history of the town and surrounding region. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Right. I’ll tell her. You can’t always find that sort of thing on the internet. Now in the old library there used to be a separate room with reference books. It was a really nice quiet room.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes. We’ve put those books in the main part of the library now, but we do have a room called the community room. It can be hired out for meetings, but at other times people can use it to study. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: I might use that. It’s hard to find anywhere quiet at home sometimes.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: I can’t remember how old your son and daughter are ... we’ve introduced a special section of fiction written specially for teenagers [[ ]] , but they might be a bit young for that?

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Yes, they would be. —————-

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Well, we do have lots of activities for younger children.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Yes?

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: For example we have a Science Club. At the next meeting, they’re going to be doing experiments with stuff that everyone has in the kitchen [[ ]] – sugar and flour and so on.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: They might be interested, yes.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: And we have a competition for children called Reading Challenge. That doesn’t begin until after the end of term. They have to read six books, and they get a certificate if they manage it.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: So that gives them something to do while they’re on holiday, instead of getting bored.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: That’s the idea. And there’s special activities for adults too. On Friday we have a local author called Tanya Streep who’s going to be talking about her new novel. It’s called ‘Catch the Mouse’ and she based the story on a crime that actually took place here years ago. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Right. We’re not free on Friday, but I’ll took out for the book.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Now this probably isn’t for you, but we do have IT support available for members. We get quite a few older people coming along who are wanting to get up to speed with computer technology. It’s on Tuesday mornings – they don’t need to make an appointment or anything, they just turn up. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Well, my mother might be interested, I’ll let her know.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: OK. And there’s another service which you wouldn’t expect from a library, which is a free medical check-up. The hospital arranges for someone to come along and measure the level of sugar in your blood, and they check cholesterol levels at the same time. [[ ]]

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Really?

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes, but that’s only for the over-60s, so you wouldn’t qualify.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: OK. Well, I’ll tell my mother, she might be interested.

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: What other information ... well, we do have a little shop with things like wallcharts and greetings cards, and also stamps [[ ]] so you can post the cards straightaway, which is really useful.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Yeah. Well, I’ll bring the children round at the weekend and we’ll join. Oh, one more thing – I’ll be bringing the car, is there parking available? [[ ]]

segments.speaker: SUSIE
segments.en: Yes, and it’s free in the evening and at weekends.

segments.speaker: PAUL
segments.en: Perfect. Well, thanks, Susie see you ...
